latest.title: Kiro diseña, Claude Code ejecuta, yo apruebo: specs como contrato y agentes de código con lista blanca
latest.description: Cuando los créditos se acabaron, separé diseño de ejecución: las specs en Kiro, cada tarea en un agente acotado de Claude Code, y un tablero que lee la spec sin tocarla. Lo que encontró una revisión cruzada antes de que existiera el tablero, y lo que el tablero no resuelve.

latest.title: Zero single points of failure, Part 1: contribution to packaging on AWS
latest.description: How to build redundancy into the first three stages of a low-latency live streaming pipeline on AWS: redundant SRT contribution feeds, dual-pipeline encoding in AWS Elemental MediaLive, and dual-ingest packaging in AWS Elemental MediaPackage V2. Part 2 covers capacity planning, delivery, and testing.

latest.description: I turned a small Tanzanian shop into a 24/7 business using Lambda, Bedrock, DynamoDB and WhatsApp. No servers, no big budget — just $1.20/month. Here's the exact architecture and code.

latest.title: Freestyle Job vs Declarative Pipeline in Jenkins: Which One Should You Use?
latest.description: When I started learning Jenkins on AWS, the first question I hit was: “Should I create a Freestyle job or a Pipeline?” Both can build and deploy your code, but they work very differently. In this article I explain both in simple terms, compare them, and help you decide which one to use on your EC2-hosted Jenkins server.

latest.title: Building a Secure Cloud Network on AWS: A Hands-On Challenge with Public and Private Subnets
latest.description: A hands-on AWS networking challenge demonstrating how to design and implement a secure cloud network using Amazon VPC, public and private subnets, Internet Gateways, route tables, NAT Gateways, and security groups. This step-by-step guide covers network configuration, connectivity testing, and AWS networking best practices.

trending.title: Can AI agents escape a Lambda MicroVM sandbox? Strands Box prevented it.
trending.description: AI agents are starting to act outside the lines they are given, so I tested the worst case: I put one in a Lambda MicroVM and told it to escape, with 13 techniques from current security research. The microVM boundary held the flag, the credentials and the control plane on its own, but the agent still tunnelled data out over DNS. A Strands-Box-style policy stopped that too, blocking 44 of 49 moves and cutting sensitive exposure from 9 kinds to 0.

trending.title: Orchestrating Agents: Nobody Decides Who Goes Next
trending.description: In a Strands swarm, routing is a model's tool call and termination is silence. Real runs against strands-agents 1.63.0 show what 'completed' actually means: nobody asked for help.

trending.title: Will AWS Emulator Replace the AWS Blocks Mocks? What Running Both Revealed About a Third Testing Layer
trending.description: AWS Emulator reproduces AWS APIs locally, while AWS Blocks ships its own local mocks. The two replace AWS at different layers: Blocks swaps in mocks at import time, and the emulator answers SDK calls. Running the same operations against both in CI, KVStore matched the mock, and FileBucket returned the S3 behavior that DESIGN.md only describes in prose. IAM and PostgreSQL remain gaps. A contributor's reading of why the emulator fits as a third layer between the mocks and the sandbox.

trending.title: Let the Model Choose, Let Code Decide: Six Patterns for Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
trending.description: Lessons from building BrailleBridge, where nothing a model writes reaches a blind student until code or a teacher has checked it: graph nodes that compare two readers, a describe-and-check loop, interrupts that survive across AgentCore invocations, hooks that rewrite tool results, capped model calls, and evals that test the checks themselves, with the code for each.

trending.title: I Put Amazon Bedrock Guardrails in Front of My Agent. Here's What Still Got Through.
trending.description: A guardrail on the Converse call never sees tool results. I tested 50 attacks and legitimate requests in English and Slovak: the model-call guardrail caught 0 of 10 indirect injections, ApplyGuardrail on tool results caught 7, and InvokeGuardrailChecks caught 10.

trending.description: Selecting subnets in multiple Availability Zones does not increase the hourly charge for a single Transit Gateway VPC attachment. Here is how subnet selection affects connectivity, and how Transit Gateway pricing compares with VPC peering.
